purpose: Owner-review draft: Dolbur's tier-1 click-through chapter (Red herb, Blue herb, Yellow herb), written in the established Neet chapter format - chapter-pilot-neet-t1.json is the same-tier benchmark (pilot chapter-click-02). The chapter opens as soon as any material family reaches tier 1; the player picks one currently unlocked material inside the opening scene; the choice sets the route; Dolbur is dispatched; after the trip the player opens a click-through continuation carrying the journey's action, setbacks, decisions, and growth. Each route stands alone and holds the accountability arc the pack's outcome gives it: Life shows him owning the shortcut he led other feet onto, Mana shows him reading his own failure and building the answer, Stamina shows him converting a broken boast into a working plan. Nothing here edits data/, source/, or the playable HTML.

presentationModel: Player opens a tier chapter when any material family reaches that tier. Inside the opening scene the player chooses one currently unlocked tier material; that choice determines the route. Dolbur is dispatched. When the trip finishes, the player opens a click-through continuation showing what happened on the trail and the route's outcome. Other unlocked routes can be played on later trips, one active route at a time.
playerFlow: op-01 -> op-02 -> choice -> confirm = byte-exact hook box for the chosen family -> one route departure box -> trip-start (dispatch, no result) -> trip timer -> trip-end (click to open the report) -> route return boxes in order, last box = byte-exact outcome. After the chapter, other unlocked choices remain available on later trips.

implementationNotes.chapterOpen: The chapter becomes available as soon as any herb material family reaches tier 1. Suggested UI copy, outside the story beats: 'New chapter - Trailside Herb Hunt.'
implementationNotes.optionGating: Show only options for material families currently unlocked at this tier; one, two, or three options are all valid states. The opening prose is written to hold when only one option exists.
implementationNotes.routeLock: The material choice sets the active route for this trip; other unlocked choices remain available on later trips, one active route at a time.
implementationNotes.tripTimer: The trip runs about two minutes on the game timer. The timer belongs to implementation and UI, not to story text.
implementationNotes.awardHandling: The script never states or implies that the player receives the chosen herb: the herb names which journey the telling follows, not freight. source/core.js:269 awards stamps, likeability, boosts, and bonuses only - no ingredient, no herb - and the trip-end beat only opens Dolbur's report; awarding belongs to the game's existing systems, outside story text.
implementationNotes.displayModel: Current in-game flow this script mirrors: the hook for the selected family already shows as the story preview before dispatch (source/app.js:147, from the tier-1 route preview in source/core.js), and the outcome shows once after the trip (source/core.js recordExpeditionStory sections; journal at line 363). The confirm box repeats the hook, the final click-through beat repeats the outcome, and nothing pre-dispatch states outcome facts.

beatRules: Every beat carries id, phase, speaker, portrait, text. The choice beat additionally carries its note and its three option texts.

Narrator beats stay brief and set place, action, or a visible action. Dolbur carries the recognition, reasoning, and decisions in his own spoken lines; accountability comes through what he does, orders, and re-ties - never through mood labels. No route side character speaks: no accepted journey draft exists for Dolbur tier 1, so no dialogue is invented for the hiker or the trail carriers; each side presence stays narrator-carried with one scene function.
Each return route opens with a 'The report starts...' narrator sentence so the post-trip account runs chronologically from where the trip went.

Each box is written to be comfortable in a dialogue box: about 40 words (whitespace token audit, hard ceiling 43 for every new beat). The byte-exact hook quote (confirm) and the byte-exact outcome quote (final return box) repeat already accepted screen text and are exempt from the target.

Portrait availability (verified): speaker 'narrator' is unvoiced scene text with no portrait. Speaker 'dolbur' shows the Dolbur portrait ('dolbur' - source/core.js TRAVELERS line 12 'DolburPortrait.png'; file assets/characters/DolburPortrait.webp). No other speaker beats exist: the hiker and the yard's carriers stay narrator-carried, so no 'none-new-side-character' beat appears in this chapter.
No outcome fact appears anywhere before the trip ends. Pre-dispatch boxes carry only hook facts and Dolbur's spoken intentions.

Aftermath wording stays owned by the final byte-exact outcome beats (the splint kit check, the clinic's 'finest invention', his 'overdue paperwork'; the decoy's spread from base camp to base camp; the three-trip walk-back rhythm becoming trail standard). Scene beats show the same journey facts in scene time in their own words; the ownership scan verifies zero outcome-phrase reuse in non-final beats.

Route independence: no beat assumes another route was seen, no cross-route character appearances, no Neet-route assumptions, no tier-2 references, no later-tier references, and no customs recited outside the byte-exact outcome beats. Each of the three routes stands alone and reads cleanly in any play order.
Award discipline: no beat states or implies the player receives the chosen herb; the trip's rewards belong to the game's existing settlement systems outside story text (source/core.js:269).

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The trailside herb jobs are waiting this morning, and the herb work is Dolbur's.

beats.speaker: dolbur
beats.text: Trail day! Boots, pack frame, and rope, all checked by hand this morning. Point me at the herb, and I will make the trip worth talking about.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Choose which herb sends Dolbur out.
beats.note: Only options whose material family is unlocked at this tier are shown. The opening prose above is written to hold whether one option or three are available. The chosen herb names the journey this telling follows; it is the story's focus, never a settlement award.

options.teaser: The clinic's red order is urgent, and Dolbur's known shortcut is technically a trail.
Birds are working the blue patch from the air, and the assigned defense is one loud voice.
The yellow bundles are heavier than they look, and a single-trip record has already been announced.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: Dolbur takes the assignment and goes; whatever happens out there comes home with him.

sharedDispatch.speaker: narrator
sharedDispatch.text: The trip is over. Open Dolbur's report to see what happened, and how it ended.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The trail clinic wants red herbs, and Dolbur knows a shortcut that is technically a trail. He is halfway down it already.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: Red herbs, then! The shortcut is the shorter line, and I have run it plenty of times without complaint. The clinic will have its red well before the kettle sings.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the fork, reached twice: Dolbur had dropped halfway down the shortcut alone, then climbed back when a hiker - out for the day and glad of company that knows the hill - turned up at the sign.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Confident from the test run, he offered the faster line - his boots had just proved it - and the hiker took it, pace set by the boots ahead.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The far ledge was the shortcut's honest half: shelf rock with nobody's care on it, a crossing only his boots had ever learned. The step there that held his weight all season went loose under an ankle it had never met.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The hiker went down hard on the shelf, hands first, ankle swelling in the time a step takes twice. The line had made his offer sound safe; now it had to own the difference.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: The report comes first, and it is mine: my shortcut, my line, and a crossing stone nobody tends. The ankle turned on all three. I am sorry. Hold still - the carry is mine, and the splint waits at the clinic.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Then he went back over the same crossing with a passenger: the hiker up on his back, every step on the line his own boots knew, and the apology running under it the whole way - low, steady, and pointed at himself.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: At the clinic, the splint came third: board, wrap, and strap set by his own hands at the senior's word. Then the desk got the same report he gave on the ledge - shortcut named, crossing named, fault taken twice.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The evening went into his kit: splint board first, then wraps, tape, a spare cord, and the list pinned where his hands could find it without asking his memory. That afternoon the only splint board in reach had belonged to the clinic.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: A hiker's ankle turns on the far ledge, and the shortcut is the reason. He reports the wrong turn first, carries them back second, splint third, apology throughout. Every hunt after starts with a splint kit check, which the town clinic calls his finest invention and he calls overdue paperwork.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The blue-herb patch by the trail head is being raided bird by bird, and Dolbur has been assigned six rows to defend with his voice.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: Blue herbs, then! Six rows, one voice, and an assignment I cannot refuse: I am the defense. The birds are about to get the loudest afternoon the patch has ever heard.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts on the watch: he opened the defense at a volume that carries across three fields, calling the six rows to order one by one and declaring every leaf's interest to the whole valley.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The birds came anyway, and they came on a timetable: every raid ran in the pause after a bellow. By the third pass it was plain - the noise had edges, and the raid lived in them.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: Ha - my own timetable, reading me back! Fine: the volume ends, and a rival takes its place. Give me the rag - the red one, off the kit - and every carrot green going spare. Their schedule has company coming.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He built the rival standing up: greens bundled loud and bright, the rag's red end flying from the knot, posted one fence post over from the rows where the raiders would have to pick a side.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Then the test: a raid dropped off the rail, caught the rag in its eye, and turned in one body. The six rows kept their leaf end to end - defended, that hour, by something that would hold still.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: He let the evening finish it: two passersby asked, and he walked them through rag, greens, and knot step by step, then sent them off with spare greens and a dare.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: Shouting only teaches the birds to wait, so he ties a decoy bundle - carrot tops, red rag, plenty of cheer - and the birds mob that instead. The patch survives, and the decoy trick spreads from base camp to base camp.

confirmBeats.speaker: narrator
confirmBeats.text: The yellow-herb bundles are heavier than they look, and Dolbur has announced he will carry the biggest one in a single trip.

departureBeats.speaker: dolbur
departureBeats.text: Yellow herbs, then! The big bundle rides my back, and the yard heard me say the word 'single' out loud. The ropes get tied at full stretch - the way my shoulders like them.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The report starts at the loading yard: the big bundle went on his back tied at a pull that made the yard's older shoulders whistle, and it held beautifully - for exactly as far as the last of the flat.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The snap came at the switchback in two voices - the belly line first, then the shoulder rope. The bundles let go down the slope, scattering yellow leaf over the grass, and nothing worth keeping was hurt except the announcement.

returnBeats.speaker: dolbur
returnBeats.text: Two ropes gone, one announcement left. Fine: the boast re-ties first, then the rope. The yard was promised delivery, not carry. The big load splits into three trips, each tied to what a rope bears.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The salvage came first: both snapped lengths picked up off the slope, the injured ends cut clean, the good parts bound into one honest working line. A broken rope, he said, is a job with a beginning and an end.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The new rule: a line earns its load by proving itself. Shorter than it started, it walked the switchback twice with nothing aboard, came back unchanged, and only then got handed something that mattered.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The split held: three loads under the rope's honest limit, walked in order with breath at the yard between trips. The two other carriers working the same switchback watched one round and split their own bundles before the afternoon ran out.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: At the gate he delivered the yard its herbs in three working loads and told the count himself: the single-carry promise failed and got named; the delivery promise held, and the thanks he earned that evening he did not argue with.

returnBeats.speaker: narrator
returnBeats.text: The ropes snap, and something in him snaps politely along with them. He repairs cheerfully and splits the load into three trips; the three-trip walk-back rhythm becomes how the trail shares heavy loads.

skillStages.planning: planning.md outputs restated for the Dolbur tier-1 chapter: the approved tier-1 chapter shape (opening -> choice -> hook confirm -> departure -> dispatch -> return beats -> outcome), with one deviation documented: no accepted journey draft exists for Dolbur tier 1, so the continuation between hook and outcome is planned as new fan-written scene work to the outcome's own action order, and the in-between beats exist to stage decisions already implied by the outcome. POV limits: pre-dispatch boxes may state hook facts and Dolbur's spoken intentions only - no result. Each route's return is a chronological report ('The report starts...'), so the account runs forward from the trip's first scene. The report-first mandate (user directive) drives Life's beat order; the observe-then-devise mandate drives Mana's; the active-split mandate drives Stamina's.
skillStages.drafting: dialogue-and-behavior.md governs the boxes: Dolbur's lines are energetic and direct (established anchor: 'An energetic warrior who approaches adventures with plenty of enthusiasm'; the job description's 'another energetic adventure'), while the accountability beats are staged as action orders - a report he gives before carrying anyone, a rival he builds on purpose, a boast he re-ties before a rope. No side-character dialogue invented: the hiker reacts in body (the sit-down, the carried ride), the birds answer in behavior (the timetable, the turned flock), the carriers adopt in one afternoon. The end of each route is the accepted outcome beat, so each route ends with the pack's own claim.
skillStages.reviewing: revision-checklist pass on all three click-throughs: choice causality, no pre-dispatch outcome disclosure, route independence (no cross-route characters, no Neet-route assumptions, no tier-2 references, no outcome recitation outside the byte-exact beats), character anchoring (the hiker enters with role and first impression; the birds are a behaving flock, not scenery; the carriers are present witness with one function), voice consistency (Dolbur in the same register in every spoken box), box economy, and mapping completeness (each outcome's action order shows fully in the scene before the final quote).

characterNotes.dolbur: Tier-1 Dolbur is the established warrior at the start of his habits: energetic, direct, and not yet checking his plan for other feet. The routes give him the beginning of the later accountability and practicality: he names his own line as the cause (Life), reads a failure off the birds instead of shouting harder (Mana), and re-ties the boast before the rope (Stamina). His tier-5 viewpoint material (the nest watch, the coin practice, the bent piton) belongs to the shared event and is not borrowed here. Portrait: 'dolbur' (verified: source/core.js TRAVELERS line 12 'DolburPortrait.png'; file assets/characters/DolburPortrait.webp).
characterNotes.hiker: Life route only, unnamed; out for a day's walk, glad of company that knows the hill, and the accountability's receiver. Enters with role and first impression; never speaks; carried back on Dolbur's back per the outcome. No portrait asset in the game's established set (checked the TRAVELERS roster in source/core.js and assets/characters/); narrator-carried.
characterNotes.patchRaiders: Mana route only: a behaving flock, not scenery. They arrive on a timetable, teach the watch to fail, and turn as one body when the rival goes up; the outcome owns their learned waiting and the decoy's spread. Unnamed by design. No speaker beat.
characterNotes.trailCarriers: Stamina route only, unnamed; the yard's older shoulders and the two carriers on the same switchback. Purposeful as the adoption witnesses - they split their own bundles the same day after watching one round. The outcome owns the lasting custom. No speaker beat.
